action_history.rationale: Approach: Refine the prior vaterite count by improving recall with a scale-space LoG blob detector sized to the ~140 px disc diameter and shape-filtered to exclude the dark elongated debris, then measure the size distribution in pixels (calibration untrusted).

result.detailed_analysis:
The image shows a bright-field optical micrograph containing two morphologically distinct populations: (1) round, fringed, birefringent discs with a bright central spot — consistent with vaterite spherulites viewed face-on — and (2) dark, elongated, lens/ellipsoid-shaped objects (either edge-on discs or debris). The analysis attempted to count and size only the round vaterite discs, reporting 24 'individual round discs' with a median diameter of 140.6 px. However, both the quality metrics and direct visual inspection of the overlay reveal a detection-coupling failure: several clearly visible bright fringed discs (e.g. in the left and lower-center of the image) are unmarked, while several dark elongated debris/edge-on objects were accepted. This means the reported population is NOT a clean sample of face-on vaterite discs, undermining both the count (24) and the shape-purity claim.

The size distribution is the most physically informative and most concerning feature. It is clearly BIMODAL, not the expected unimodal near-monodisperse distribution: a dominant cluster at ~140 px (15 particles, diameters 137–161 px, tight std, aspect ratio ~1.0–1.1, solidity ~0.99 — genuine round discs) and a distinct secondary cluster at ~110 px (9 particles, diameters 95–125 px). Critically, the small-mode particles have elevated aspect ratios (1.32–1.73) and reduced minor axes (73–110 px), i.e. they are elongated, not round. These are almost certainly the dark lens-shaped debris/edge-on discs that leaked through the shape filter — their smaller apparent 'diameter' is an artifact of being elongated ellipses rather than a true second size population. So the bimodality reflects contamination by a morphologically different object class, not a real bimodal size distribution of vaterite. The clean upper mode (~140 px, aspect ratio ≈1.0, solidity ≈0.99) is the defensible measurement of the true face-on disc size.

Calibration was correctly flagged as unusable: the metadata pixel size (80.566 nm/px) implies ~10.9 µm discs, which is implausibly large for these few-micron vaterite spherulites, and back-computation assuming ~5 µm discs gives ~37 nm/px — a 54% disagreement. No defensible nm/µm conversion exists, so all sizes remain in pixels. The count (24) and the size distribution must therefore be interpreted as low-confidence, relative (pixel-based) measurements, with the round-disc mode being the only well-supported physical result.

scientific_claims.claim: The genuine face-on vaterite discs form a near-monodisperse population with a diameter of ~140 px (137–161 px, ~15 particles), aspect ratio ≈1.0–1.1 and solidity ≈0.99, while an apparent secondary size mode at ~110 px is an artifact of elongated (aspect ratio 1.3–1.7) lens-shaped objects that leaked through the shape filter rather than a true second population of vaterite.
scientific_claims.scientific_impact: Distinguishing a real size mode from a contamination artifact is essential for correctly characterizing vaterite monodispersity; treating the bimodality as physical would overstate polydispersity and misrepresent the synthesis outcome. The high solidity/circularity of the upper mode confirms the round discs are compact spherulites viewed face-on.
scientific_claims.has_anyone_question: Has anyone shown that apparent bimodality in optically imaged vaterite disc size distributions arises from mixing face-on (round) and edge-on/elongated projections rather than a true bimodal particle population?

issues.location: Dark elongated debris throughout the image (e.g. top-left cluster, mid-left, bottom-right pairs)
issues.problem: The shape filter did NOT reliably exclude dark elongated debris; the accepted-disc overlay includes several dark lens/elongated objects rendered as accepted discs (e.g. the orange-brown object mid-right, several tan/olive objects). The plan explicitly required NO marks on dark elongated debris.

issues.location: Discness feature contradiction (working texture/rim map, bottom-left panel)
issues.problem: The 'discness' map lights up BOTH the bright vaterite discs AND the dark elongated debris (both show bright rims), so LoG on this map cannot separate them by intensity — separation is left entirely to the shape filter, which is leaking.

Distribution is clearly bimodal: a main mode at ~140 px and a spurious secondary mode at ~110-115 px. The lower mode corresponds to the leaked elongated debris / partial lobes (equivalent-circle diameters of elongated objects), not true discs.

N_detected=24 is within the 26-30 ±20% band numerically, but ~6-9 of those 24 are debris false positives while several genuine round discs are missed, so the true recall of discs is lower than the number implies.

verification_iterations.fix_applied: Enforce the stated shape filter (drop the 6-7 objects with aspect_ratio>1.35 or solidity<0.9) and add an interior-discness/intensity gate so dark elongated debris interiors score low; recompute the histogram — the ~110 px secondary mode should collapse to leave a unimodal ~140 px distribution.
